findings.title: MHFE Check verdict is not bound to its current fields
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The current fields can receive a recovery assurance that belongs to an obsolete fingerprint; resolve before publishing the affected Check workflow.
findings.reproduction: Run the real Check tab with a synthetic successful check; defer only the final walletParameters request, edit the fingerprint, then resolve parameters.
findings.expected: Editing clears the old assurance and its late completion cannot certify current fields.
findings.observed: A fingerprint edited while final walletParameters waits is followed by Matches for the old fingerprint.
findings.impact: Misleading recovery rehearsal for the current written backup/reference. This is verdict attribution, not an incorrect cryptographic comparison.
findings.recommendedFix: Recheck input revision after final parameters resolve, immediately before result mutation; preserve no-length answer events as job questions.
findings.requiredVerification: Replay the bounded real-tab deferred-parameters regression, plus unchanged completion and Cancel/reset variants of Encode/New wallet.

findings.title: MHFE Cancel before client preparation does not prevent later work
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Bounded attribution/cancellation defect; no incorrect cipher output or direct key compromise demonstrated. Fix before presenting the affected recovery flow as fully verified.
findings.evidence: late-publication-complete-fixture: second failed test; independent shared-flow source challenge
findings.reproduction: Run the real rekey tab with a complete synthetic sealed result; defer only seal's coreParameters request, press its visible Cancel button, then resolve parameters.
findings.expected: Cancellation remains latched through final metadata and prevents subsequent card/status publication.
findings.observed: Cancel during the final NewContainerResult.seal metadata wait still leads to Password changed in 0 s. Encode/New wallet have the same shared source path.
findings.impact: The cancelled recovery operation can still publish a verified card and success for its captured inputs. This reproduction occurs after synthetic cryptographic work completed; it does not demonstrate new KDF work after Cancel, a wrong container or external secret disclosure.
findings.recommendedFix: Guard the result lifetime inside seal after its await and before any DOM mutation, invalidate it on reset, and guard caller success. Merely racing the caller with run.step does not revoke seal's internal mutations.
findings.requiredVerification: Replay the bounded real-tab deferred-parameters regression, plus unchanged completion and Cancel/reset variants of Encode/New wallet.

findings.title: Public export completion is not consistently bound to its result snapshot

evidence.method: Read-only source inspection; regression files read, not executed
evidence.sourceBinding: Current per-file SHA-256 values in sourceBindings; no whole-snapshot verification claim
evidence.executedFollowup: scanner-export-generation: both normal-scan stale reply variants fail the expected contract; integrated Activity coin transition remains source-only.

reproduction.case: Scanner broker reply after a new normal scan
reproduction.prerequisites: A completed normal seed/watch-only scan has a staged public report; the user requests its export and the broker reply is delayed.
steps: Start an export of scan A; downloadExport captures runGeneration=G and awaits the broker.
Start a fresh normal seed or watch-only scan B. openRun clears the staging and results but does not increment runGeneration.
Let scan A's broker resolve or reject while B is active or complete. Its captured generation still equals G, so the old reply updates B's status/error.

reproduction.case: Activity workbook crosses the Dash/external result owners
reproduction.prerequisites: Full Activity app includes an external coin; a completed Dash result remains in the Dash controller's currentExport; the local workbook promise is deferred.
steps: Begin XLSX of Dash result A. The exporter retains A and sets export busy; query-running remains false, so Coin and new queries remain usable.

Select Bitcoin or Ethereum and complete an external lookup B. The external controller updates its own exportState and the shared result/status view. It never clears the Dash controller's currentExport.
Resolve or reject workbook A. dependencies.state() still returns A, so the Dash exporter accepts the stale success/error. Its finally also writes shared export controls.

findings.expected: Export publication and feedback remain bound to the visible result/scan owner through Clear and replacement.
observed: No generation change exists in openRun or its normal seed/watch-only callers. Address-search prepareRun increments the generation, but that is a different path.

app.ts installs both owners on one view. External configure/submit/capture handlers modify only external exportState; the Dash controller has no Coin-change subscription or cross-owner invalidation. setExportBusy does not set query-running or lock Coin.
impact: Stale public status/error attribution; an already authorized shell download is not shown to be revoked or unsafe.

An old public Dash workbook may download and overwrite the current external result's feedback. The reverse direction also lacks a guaranteed ownership check when returning to Dash; it was not separately developed as a reproduction. No private data leak is alleged.
findings.recommendedFix: Advance Scanner export generation on every new run; invalidate or qualify Activity exports across the Dash/external owners, including shared-control finalization.
requiredVerification: Deferred successful and rejected broker replies after a new normal seed/watch-only scan, through the actual controller. Increment or otherwise replace the export identity on every new run.

Use both production owners on one memory view, defer Dash workbook success/rejection, switch to a completed external result, and assert no old publication/status/error or ownership-inappropriate finalization. Qualify by a shared host result identity or explicitly invalidate the inactive owner's export.

mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: MhfeTask owns the heavy-job gate, AwaitingAnswer disposition, package-error presentation and optional session hold. MhfeRun latches Cancel and suppresses late results of operations passed to step(). Actual vendor WorkerJob ignores replies after termination and OperationSlot releases the long job on its result.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: The operation as a whole is not raced or guarded. ends.current only controls error presentation. It does not protect arbitrary success mutations inside a caller.

mhfeSupportedContracts.contract: Password review and strength helper invalidation
mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: PasswordReview drops an old asynchronous review after reset/input revision, conceals and clears answers, revokes handed-out choices through a WeakSet, and exposes assertCurrent. StrengthNote drops stale estimates.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: Written helper tests were inspected, not run. Correct helper invalidation does not establish that every consuming tab asserts the reviewed choice after its own awaits.

mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: Encode reads phrase facts through the actual MhfeClient; Decode reads canonical container facts then decrypts with those facts. New wallet draws through MhfeWallet and encrypts the returned phrase. Marked-container and Repair delegate inspection/repair to MhfeRepair; missing words delegates search candidates and search operations to the core. Marked-container acceptance writes the returned container and emits change before resuming.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: Trace of public operations and data ownership only. No cryptographic known-answer result, search completeness, WASM provenance or checked-generator result was independently verified.

mhfeSupportedContracts.contract: Phrase-length offer and repair profile ownership
mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: PhraseLengthChoice populates package word counts and adapts to container phraseLengths, builtInCheckLengths and confirmationFor. Decode adapts again at operation start. Repair output profile/capacity facts are read from the package result rather than recomputed.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: Native select behavior and stale adaptation ordering are unexecuted. No-length semantics are excluded. Static HTML limits/options still duplicate metadata as recorded below.

mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: New wallet captures the exact passphrase string, sends it to drawPhrase and retains it in renderPhrase/useMnemonicInDeriver. The handoff assigns the given string without trim/case fold. Hidden-wallet handoff does not forward the main wallet screening passphrase. Vendored clients encode password/passphrase strings for public WASM APIs; upstream Password and wallet passphrase ownership apply NFKD. Password repeated input is compared before review/repair.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: Exact passphrase handoff preserves the original string; normalization belongs to the library. Unicode differential/native-browser parity was not tested. A reviewed-choice/current-input race remains below.

mhfeSupportedContracts.contract: Hidden session error disposition and cleanup
mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: Frontend error retention reads hiddenWalletRefusals from core parameters. The actual worker uses the same library parameter list, with nine upstream refusal codes; other errors end its session. AwaitingAnswer is a frontend review wait. Normal close clears references, fields, review, display and timer, and releases the page gate in finally around session.close. Blur/hidden concealment does not create a wallet list or copy action.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: Cleanup on failed classification-parameter retrieval is not guaranteed. No runtime secret erasure, native isolation or browser memory wiping claim is made.

mhfeSupportedContracts.contract: Both Argon2 engines and fast mode are retained
mhfeSupportedContracts.supported: MhfeEngine constructs MhfeClient with both threaded and single-threaded source texts. Mode selection still follows crossOriginIsolated and the actual client chooses the corresponding source. Both engine files are present and their current SHA-256 values are recorded.
mhfeSupportedContracts.limit: Engine files were hashed for presence, not audited internally or executed. Fast-mode performance/thread behavior and equality of native/browser outputs remain unverified. No cryptographic parameters were changed.

unexecutedSourceFollowups.observed: The heavy gate disables marked action buttons but leaves input edits available. Encode/New wallet/Decode do not bind whole-operation success to input/source revisions. Linked-source main Clear emits recovery-source-change but Encode does not revoke its captured phrase operation. MissingWords input changes revoke only the long-search confirmation; hide/back clears fields without cancelling the run. Marked-container input hides its block but lacks a response revision. Quick Repair likewise has no edit-bound result revision. Decode's asynchronous change adaptation may also apply obsolete length offers, although its operation re-reads/adapts the container.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.limit: A cleared/hidden block may receive a late result in hidden DOM; visibility was not tested. Main Clear reachability assumes the MHFE source is linked and already captured. No wrong cryptographic value is alleged.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.neededCoordinatorEvidence: Actual tab event matrix for field edits, linked main Clear and missing-words back/hide during deferred facts/work/metadata, with unchanged-input controls.

unexecutedSourceFollowups.status: consumer source gap; original helper remediation remains separately supported
unexecutedSourceFollowups.observed: Hidden open obtains ReviewChoice, awaits progress(), then reads live password/repeat with the old choice without assertCurrent. Encode uses captured password/choice after its progress await without assertCurrent. New wallet asserts a pre-draw choice only after displaying the drawn phrase, then its encrypt method crosses client/progress awaits without a final assertion. Field edits can revoke the helper's choice without those consumers observing revocation.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.limit: The library validates its request and refuses unsupported repairs. The source gap concerns attribution of an accepted review choice and old-input publication, not a demonstrated authentication bypass. This does not replace or duplicate the original AUD-022-UI002 finding about reappearing helper choices.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.neededCoordinatorEvidence: Delay progress/metadata after a reviewed choice; edit either repeated field; verify no old choice is accepted with new live text and no old-input completion appears.

unexecutedSourceFollowups.observed: Hidden open's catch awaits a fresh coreParameters request before calling close for a fatal/cancel error. If that quick parameters request rejects, catch exits into finally, which only reenables Open. Frontend #session/#endSession, session UI and held heavy gate are not disposed by that path; normal explicit/idle close remains available.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.limit: Parameter-read failure was not injected. The backend may already have terminated its worker; this is not proof of retained native/Argon2 secret memory. Ordinary documented refusal disposition is correctly delegated.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.neededCoordinatorEvidence: Reject classification parameters after a fatal/cancelled session.open; assert frontend session teardown and gate release, plus documented-refusal keep-open control.

unexecutedSourceFollowups.observed: HTML repeats PIM max 1023 and repair count/capacity options. Password UI repeats check-word count 5, defaults 5/16 and weak threshold/entropy messages; NewPasswordChoice repeats default recipe counts/text. The common password count input advertises max 64 for word and character kinds, while the upstream recipe permits at most 32 words and 64 characters. The passwords module exposes metadata via parameters, but this UI does not adapt its bounds from it.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.limit: Package validation still rejects incompatible values. Static preset choices may be intentional UI selections, but thresholds/limits/profile descriptions have duplicate owners. Not a complete evaluation or closure of the original 13-family architecture finding.
unexecutedSourceFollowups.neededCoordinatorEvidence: Populate limits/profile text from parameter/error owners; verify kind-specific count bounds and avoid new frontend copies.

limitations: Review depth is source inspection plus bounded regressions, not independent security certification, complete cryptographic correctness or release readiness.

No deliberate release/full-vector/KDF/browser/Docker/native/WASM/PDF-rendering procedure was requested. Initial merged harness configuration could widen test selection; it timed out at 90 seconds with only the Vitest banner retained, was interrupted, and no outcome is accepted from it. Exact one-file scoped reruns replaced it.
Node heap ceiling 1536 MiB, one test worker, checks sequential. Memory sample: 7961620480 bytes used, 7857393664 bytes available. No continuous global peak guarantee across other sessions.

Source changed concurrently. Command records bind stable intervals; whole-review baseline and final fingerprints differ. Historical audit metadata also changed externally; no retrospective rerun of old evidence is implied.
Four copy-check test failures are not confirmed product defects: a trivial child subprocess also produces EPERM in this execution environment.
The first scoped Rekey fixture omitted result fields and misleadingly passed after a rendering error; it was corrected, and only the complete-fixture failure is accepted.

Seven AUD-024 findings have bounded regression verification; DOC001 is source-fixed; six remain open/partial. No signed remediation commits exist for this follow-up; exact source hashes substitute for commit identity.

Actual frontend versus native cryptographic equality, randomness distributions, all error paths, runtime secret erasure, fast-mode performance and emitted artifacts are not established by synthetic clients or source hashes.
No production edits, other-project edits, commits, pushes, tags, releases, remote CI or messages were performed by this review.
Exact model snapshot and reasoning setting are unavailable; user UI labels are not substituted for execution metadata.
